ai.description: Horsfield's Spiny Lizard reaches 25 cm. It is brownish-grey with dark crossbands and a pale throat. Distinctive features include a prominent nuchal crest and sharp, keeled scales on the body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Salea horsfieldii* is best distinguished by the prominent, elongated nuchal crest of enlarged, lanceolate scales that extend down the back, unlike the smaller crests of other *Salea*.
ai.habitat: *Salea horsfieldii* inhabits high-altitude montane shola forests and adjacent grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Horsfield's Spiny Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively basking on rocks or tree trunks to regulate its body temperature before foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Salea horsfieldii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Salea horsfieldii* is endemic to the high-elevation shola grasslands and forests of the Western Ghats in southern India, typically found above 1,500 meters.
